Severe Flooding Hits Indonesian Real Estate Industry, Disrupting Operations and Damaging Sites

A wave of severe flooding in Indonesia’s West Java province has caused widespread disruption to the real estate industry, with multiple firms reporting significant damage to properties, ongoing construction projects, and business premises. The event, triggered by days of torrential rainfall, is impacting key urban and suburban areas, including Bekasi and Karawang, where many real estate developments are concentrated.

Industry sources indicate that at least 18 residential and commercial developments owned by leading firms such as Nusantara Realty and Citra Land Group have been inundated, with ground floors submerged and basements completely flooded. “We are facing substantial losses as several of our ongoing projects are under water, halting all progress and jeopardizing the safety of our on-site staff,” said Ari Wibowo, spokesperson for Nusantara Realty.

The Indonesian Real Estate Association (APERSI) estimates that over 2,000 workers have been affected, with many evacuated from high-risk zones. “Our main concern is the safety of employees and residents, as well as the integrity of partially completed structures,” said APERSI chairwoman Sinta Pranata. She noted that while no casualties have been reported among the workforce, the full extent of property damage will only become clear once floodwaters recede.

Developers are currently assessing the impact on their assets and considering temporary relocation of employees whose offices have been rendered inaccessible. The financial toll is expected to be significant, with initial projections from analysts at Jakarta-based Equity Focus suggesting direct damages could exceed $40 million in the coming weeks.

With rain still forecast for the region, real estate firms remain on high alert, closely monitoring their sites and prioritizing safety protocols. “This is an unprecedented situation for our industry,” said Wibowo. “Our immediate focus is on minimizing further risk while planning for recovery.”
